title: WP Rocket vs LiteSpeed Cache
description: A documentation-led comparison centered on the hosting constraint behind two popular WordPress performance tools.
metaDescription: A transparently scoped WP Rocket versus LiteSpeed Cache comparison from KreativWP.
comparisonAreas: Dynamic-page exclusions for ecommerce and memberships
A repeatable performance test with one cache plugin at a time
takeaway: Hosting is the first decision: LiteSpeed Cache’s caching features depend on LiteSpeed or QUIC.cloud, while WP Rocket is positioned as a paid page-cache choice for other stacks. Do not run two full-page cache plugins together.

rows.label: Cost boundary
rows.left: Paid page-cache product. Confirm the current license and renewals on the official site.
rows.right: Free WordPress plugin; optional QUIC.cloud services have their own usage and billing boundaries.

rows.label: Cache prerequisite
rows.left: Plugin-managed page caching is documented; check host compatibility before adding it to a managed cache setup.
rows.right: Full-page cache requires a supported LiteSpeed server or QUIC.cloud. Optimization features alone do not prove that page caching is active.

rows.label: Unknown hosting
rows.left: Do not buy by default. Ask the host which caching layer already exists and whether this plugin is supported.
rows.right: Do not assume that installing the plugin supplies the required server-side cache.

rows.label: Store and member pages
rows.left: Test cart, checkout, accounts, and personalized content exclusions before launch.
rows.right: Validate exclusions and cache behavior for cart, checkout, accounts, and personalized content.

sources.label: LiteSpeed Cache server requirements and features

migration: Disable the old full-page cache, remove its stale rules according to its instructions, clear server/CDN caches, and test dynamic pages before comparing cold and warm responses. Use the same host, content, and image strategy. There is no measured speed winner in this comparison.

decisionGuide.chooseLeft: the host supports it, no overlapping page-cache layer is needed, and a paid workflow is acceptable.
decisionGuide.chooseRight: LiteSpeed or QUIC.cloud page caching is confirmed and its workflow fits the site.
decisionGuide.verify: If hosting is unknown or already provides page caching, ask the host first. Use one full-page cache and verify dynamic-page exclusions.
